# Langfuse Provider

Manage Langfuse organizations, projects, API keys, memberships, and LLM connections with Terraform or OpenTofu. Organization management requires an Enterprise-enabled Langfuse instance and an admin API key. Project, membership, blob storage integration, and organization LLM connection resources use organization-scoped keys; LLM connections, annotation queues, datasets, dataset items, evaluation rules, evaluators, models, prompts, score configs, and skills use project-scoped keys.

## Authentication

| Scope | Configuration | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Admin | `admin_api_key` or `LANGFUSE_ADMIN_KEY` | Organizations and organization API keys |
| Organization | `organization_public_key` and `organization_private_key` | Projects, project API keys, memberships, blob storage integrations, organization LLM connections; `langfuse_projects` and `langfuse_user` data sources |
| Project | `project_public_key` and `project_secret_key` | LLM connections, annotation queues, datasets, dataset items, evaluation rules, evaluators, models, prompts, score configs, skills; `langfuse_project`, `langfuse_prompt`, `langfuse_score_config`, and `langfuse_dataset` data sources |

`host` is configured in the provider block; it does not read `LANGFUSE_HOST`.
An Enterprise license is configured on the Langfuse server, not in this provider.

## Security and lifecycle

Sensitive attributes hide values in CLI output but still store them in state.
Use an encrypted, access-controlled state backend and do not commit state files.
API key secrets and LLM credentials cannot be recovered from the API after
creation; retain their configuration and state securely.

## Known limitations

Some Langfuse objects cannot go through the full Terraform lifecycle because
the Langfuse public API has no endpoint for it. Each affected resource page
starts with a note or warning box that states the exact behaviour.

| Resource | Limitation | What the provider does |
|---|---|---|
| `langfuse_dataset` | No delete endpoint | Destroy removes it from state with a warning; the dataset stays in Langfuse |
| `langfuse_annotation_queue` | No update or delete endpoint | Every change forces a new, renamed queue; destroy removes it from state with a warning |
| `langfuse_annotation_queue_assignment` | No read endpoint | Changes made outside Terraform are not detected; import is not supported |
| `langfuse_score_config` | No delete endpoint | Destroy archives the score config |
| `langfuse_dataset_item` | `null` does not clear `input`, `expected_output`, `metadata` | Removing one of them forces a new item |

The Terraform and OpenTofu registry listings for this fork are pending.
The historical `langfuse/langfuse` registry address refers to upstream, not
this fork. Follow the repository's local-development instructions until
publication is complete.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    langfuse = {
      source = "langfuse/langfuse" # Local development override, not a registry install.
    }
  }
}

variable "langfuse_host" {
  type        = string
  description = "Base URL of your Langfuse instance."
}

provider "langfuse" {
  host = var.langfuse_host
  # Organization management reads the admin key from LANGFUSE_ADMIN_KEY.
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `admin_api_key` (String, Sensitive) Admin API key. Only needed when managing organizations. Can also come from LANGFUSE_ADMIN_KEY.
- `host` (String) Base URI of the Langfuse instance (defaults to https://app.langfuse.com).
